records.notes: Medial denudation of both condylar and tibial articular surfaces supplies full loss with qualitative broad anatomical extent independently of unnamedIV. LateralIII and PFII have no separately defined scale or lost-thickness morphology. Osteophytes and normal PF congruence do not supply cartilage severity.

records.notes: PF lateral trochlear defect is explicitly full-depth over11mm, independently qualifying despite unnamedIII. MedialI lacks a scale or separate below-threshold morphology. Lateral meniscus/ligament normality and lateral trochlear disease do not assess lateral tibiofemoral cartilage.

evidence: Medial compartment cartilage: Confluent regions of high-grade articular cartilage loss at both sides of the weightbearing aspect of the joint, including some areas of full-thickness fissuring and associated subchondral signal changes. High-grade cartilage loss at the posterior medial femoral condyle.

Lateral compartment cartilage: Articular cartilage irregularity and high-grade cartilage loss at the weightbearing aspect of the joint with regions of full-thickness fissuring and associated subchondral signal changes.

Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Diffuse articular cartilage loss at the patella, including areas of full-thickness cartilage loss at the median ridge, medial patellar facet, and lateral patellar facet. Full-thickness chondral fissuring at the medial and lateral trochlea.
records.notes: Medial confluent loss is only called high-grade; some full-depth fissures do not quantify a qualifying deep-loss footprint. Lateral has the same missing depth/extent separation. PF diffuse loss includes full-depth areas at three locations, but the text does not state diffuse/confluent full-depth loss or the size of one qualifying deep region; do not equate distribution of multiple deep areas/fissures with a measured or explicitly broad full-depth lesion.

records.notes: Medial explicitly complete loss across the anterior and middle thirds of both opposing surfaces establishes depth and broad qualitative extent independently ofIV. Elsewhere polytopic erosions, osteophytes at all surfaces and TF/PF narrowing lack localized loss-depth/extent; do not transfer the medial complete-loss finding to lateral/PF. Meniscal extrusion and cyst measurements are unrelated to cartilage extent.
